origin.description: S3 generic for the package name of a remote. Methods for local, CRAN, and GitHub remotes read that name without installing the package.

arguments.name: remote
arguments.text: A remote object. local_remote stores a normalized path. cran_remote stores name. github_remote stores package, repo, and the other GitHub fields.
Passed to the method. The GitHub method accepts use_local and use_curl.

origin.details: The default method returns remote$repo. A local directory reads Package from DESCRIPTION. A path that is not a directory is treated as a tarball, and the name is the file name before the first underscore. A CRAN remote returns the name field. A GitHub remote returns package when that field is already set.
origin.value: A length-1 character string. The GitHub method returns NA_character_ when the DESCRIPTION cannot be read.
origin.example:
path <- tempfile()
dir.create(path)
writeLines(c("Package: foo", "Version: 1.0.0"), file.path(path, "DESCRIPTION"))
name <- remotes:::remote_package_name(remotes:::local_remote(path))
cat(paste0("remote_package_name on a local directory with Package: foo returns ", name, ".\n"))

translation.description: S3 generic for the package name of a remote. Methods for local, CRAN, and GitHub remotes read that name without installing the package.

arguments.name: remote
arguments.text: A local_remote, cran_remote, or github_remote. Any other object uses the default and reads repo.

arguments.name: kwargs
arguments.text: The GitHub method accepts use_local. use_curl is accepted and ignored.

translation.details: The default method returns repo. A local directory reads Package from DESCRIPTION. A path that is not a directory is a tarball: the name is the text before the first underscore. A CRAN remote returns name. A GitHub remote returns package when it is already set, and that branch does not use the network. use_curl does not select the curl package.
translation.value: A string. None is NA_character_ when the GitHub DESCRIPTION lookup does not return a package name.
translation.example:
import os
import tempfile
from remotes.remote import local_remote, remote_package_name
path = tempfile.mkdtemp()
with open(os.path.join(path, "DESCRIPTION"), "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as handle:
    handle.write("Package: foo\nVersion: 1.0.0\n")
name = remote_package_name(local_remote(path))
print("remote_package_name on a local directory with Package: foo returns " + name + ".")
